author: Athul Prem

matching.method: Reciprocal interpolation of Cartesian displacement at fixed y and z/thickness with each target section's native mass matrix.

all_mode_power.convention: The native complex blocks t and r map all left-incident propagating modes to outgoing propagating modes at the original physical planes. The signed flux for a unit-amplitude mode has magnitude 1 W. Both traces are dimensionless sums of the power fractions for five separate unit-power incident drives. Tr(t†t) and Tr(r†r) are invariant under unitary changes of the corresponding power-normalized input and output bases, so cross-thickness mode matching is unnecessary. Dividing each trace by five gives the power fraction for equal incoherent incident powers. The lossless closure is Tr(t†t) + Tr(r†r) = 5, or 1 for the incoherent means. Differences of the mean fractions multiplied by 100 are percentage points.

spatial_controls.scope: The parent meshes use a 400 nm central and 150 nm lead target. A null central edge ceiling denotes the parent. Changing rim resolution also regenerates the central mesh. The nested 32-segment levels preserve the hole walls, leads and port traces. Changing the layer count includes the compatible port discretization. Spatial comparisons use only sampled shared frequencies. The 997.5 MHz pair is available on the 48-segment mesh. The thin-only finer levels have no thick pair.

all_mode_power.scope: Frequencies are in Hz. The three sampled frequencies and finite spatial increments leave continuum and frequency convergence unresolved. The saved direct flux and coherent closure checks verify conservation for each finite discretization. Prior complex and weak-conversion sensitivity failures stand.

sampled_thickness_correspondence.scope: Each row follows sampled positive-flux displacement matches at one fixed frequency. Channels and roots are local to the section and frequency. The qualified focus comparison uses only the saved 100 and 200 nm device powers at their original planes. Nested contrasts also require within-thickness links from the 48-segment rim pair. The 150 nm calculation supplies uniform-section modes only. Continuous branch identity, intermediate device powers and spatial or frequency convergence remain unresolved.

scope: T and R are sums over propagating output modes, in fractions of native incident power. Mode matches connect only the sampled frequencies and keep the original physical planes. An unresolved cross-thickness entry identifies an overlap candidate without a thickness contrast. The two nested ceilings keep the 32-segment rim, lead and port traces fixed and use distinct solve platforms. The frequency samples use 48 segments per hole. The nested increments leave continuum and frequency convergence unresolved. Prior complex and weak-conversion failures stand.
